issues.t: Automatic transmission loses forward gears
issues.sym: The car revs but will not move in Drive, pulls away weakly, or slips and bangs between gears. Reverse may still work.
issues.why: The CD4E automatic in these cars has several Ford bulletins for lost forward engagement, including a snap ring that can work out of place and internal failures serious enough that Ford added units to its remanufactured exchange program.
issues.next: Check the transmission fluid level and smell. If the car will not move or keeps slipping, stop driving it and have it towed for a transmission diagnosis; a rebuild or used unit is the usual fix.

issues.t: Water pump leak or failure and overheating
issues.sym: Coolant drips near the front of the engine, a sweet smell, the temperature gauge climbing, or a growling noise from the pump.
issues.why: Ford issued bulletins for broken or leaking water pumps on these engines and a notice that the pump bearing can work loose. Once the pump leaks, the engine can overheat quickly.
issues.next: If the gauge rises toward hot, pull over and shut the engine off. Do not open a hot radiator cap. Have the cooling system pressure-tested and the pump replaced before driving far.

issues.t: Blower motor resistor can overheat and melt (recall)
issues.sym: The fan only works on some speeds, a burning plastic smell from under the dash, or a melted connector behind the glove box.
issues.why: An open circuit in the heater blower resistor can cause arcing that melts its connector and creates a fire risk. Ford recalled these cars and also extended coverage on the blower switch and resistor.
issues.next: If you smell burning plastic, turn the fan off. Ask a dealer to check your VIN for open recall work on the blower resistor.

issues.t: Rear brakes can lock up from a corroded valve (recall)
issues.sym: The rear wheels lock or skid during firm braking, and the car may feel unstable or want to swing around.
issues.why: The rear brake pressure control valves can corrode and stop limiting rear brake pressure. If both fail, the rear wheels can lock.
issues.next: Drive gently and leave extra stopping room. Have a dealer check whether the valve recall was done on your car.

issues.t: Front coil springs can break and cut a tire (recall)
issues.sym: A loud bang or clunk from the front, the car sitting lower on one corner, or a front tire that suddenly goes flat.
issues.why: The front coil springs can rust and break. A broken spring end can rub through the tire.
issues.next: If one front corner sits low or you hear a bang, slow down and have the springs checked before highway driving. Ask a dealer about the spring recall.

issues.t: Airbag light on from a faulty crash sensor (recall)
issues.sym: The airbag warning light comes on and stays on.
issues.why: A problem in the airbag sensor assembly can turn on the warning light and switch off the airbags.
issues.next: Treat a steady airbag light as a sign the airbags may not work. Have a dealer check for the recall and read the airbag codes.

issues.t: Dash, parking and tail lights can go out (recall)
issues.sym: The instrument panel lights, parking lights or tail lights stop working, sometimes on and off.
issues.why: Heat at the headlight switch can distort a terminal and open the circuit for these lights.
issues.next: Do not drive at night without working tail lights. Ask a dealer to check the headlight switch recall on your VIN.

issues.t: Accelerator cable can stick (recall)
issues.sym: The gas pedal feels sticky, slow to return, or the engine stays at high revs after you lift off.
issues.why: The throttle cable can bind, which can hold the throttle partly open.
issues.next: If the engine keeps revving, shift to Neutral, brake firmly and pull over. Have the recall checked before driving again.

issues.t: Engine may not return to idle (recall)
issues.sym: After you lift off the gas, the engine keeps running fast instead of dropping back to idle.
issues.why: A problem with the throttle cable can keep the throttle from fully closing.
issues.next: Use the brakes firmly and shift to Neutral if it happens while driving. Ask a dealer whether the throttle cable recall was done.

issues.t: Shift indicator damage can cause wrong gear selection (recall)
issues.sym: The gear indicator by the shifter is cracked or broken, and the gear shown may not match the gear the car is in.
issues.why: The shift indicator bezel can be damaged, for example by some cleaners, so the driver may select the wrong gear.
issues.next: Always confirm the car is truly in Park with the parking brake set before getting out. Have a dealer check the shifter recall.

issues.t: Ignition and Park interlock problem (recall)
issues.sym: The key may come out or the car may not be fully secured in Park when you expect it to be.
issues.why: Ford recalled some 1999 cars for not meeting the federal rule on theft protection and rollaway prevention, which governs when the key can be removed.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake and confirm Park before leaving the car. Ask a dealer whether this recall was completed.

issues.t: Seat belt buckle may not hold in a crash (recall)
issues.sym: A buckle that does not latch firmly or releases with little force.
issues.why: Some front seat belt buckles may not restrain an occupant properly in a crash.
issues.next: Test each buckle with a firm tug. Have a dealer check whether the buckle recall applies.

issues.t: Child lock label may be misleading (recall)
issues.sym: You think the rear child safety lock is on, but the rear door still opens from the inside.
issues.why: The label on the door may show the child lock positions incorrectly, so the lock may be left off.
issues.next: Check the child lock by trying the inside handle before carrying children. A dealer can replace the label.

issues.t: Radiator fan motor can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: Smoke or a hot electrical smell from the front of the engine bay, or a cooling fan that stops working.
issues.why: Too much current can overheat the cooling fan motor. In the worst case it can ignite parts nearby.
issues.next: If you see smoke from the engine bay, pull over and turn the engine off. Ask a dealer about the fan motor recall.

issues.t: Fuel filler vent hose can crack and leak (recall)
issues.sym: A strong fuel smell or fuel dripping near the rear wheel when you fill up.
issues.why: A vent hose on the fuel filler can crack and leak fuel during refueling.
issues.next: Stop filling and move away from any ignition source if you smell or see fuel. Have a dealer check the recall.

issues.t: Check engine light from clogged EGR passages
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on, sometimes with pinging or a slight loss of power. Codes point to low EGR flow.
issues.why: Carbon builds up in the exhaust gas recirculation passages and tubes, so the system cannot flow enough exhaust back into the engine.
issues.next: Have the codes read. Cleaning the EGR passages usually fixes it; the EGR valve or pressure sensor sometimes needs replacing too.

issues.t: Rough idle and stalling at idle
issues.sym: Hard cold starts, a rough or hunting idle, stalling when you come to a stop, or a hooting noise when slowing down.
issues.why: The idle air bypass valve gets dirty or wears out, so the engine cannot hold a steady idle. Ford has bulletins for cold stalls and for noise from this valve.
issues.next: Have the idle air valve and throttle body cleaned or replaced, and check for vacuum leaks at the same time.

issues.t: Lean codes from vacuum leaks
issues.sym: Check engine light with lean codes (P0171 or P0174), a rough idle, or hesitation.
issues.why: Air sneaks into the engine through cracked vacuum hoses or intake gaskets, which upsets the fuel mixture.
issues.next: Ask the shop to smoke-test the intake for leaks before replacing sensors.

issues.t: Timing belt shredding (2.0L)
issues.sym: A slapping or scraping noise from the timing belt cover, or the engine suddenly quits and will not restart.
issues.why: Ford found the 2.0L timing belt could shred or rub against its front cover. If the belt breaks, the engine stops and may be damaged.
issues.next: If you hear noise from the timing cover, have the belt inspected right away. Replace it on schedule if there is no record.

issues.t: Hard starting in freezing weather (2.0L)
issues.sym: Below freezing, the engine cranks a long time or will not start, and may smell of fuel.
issues.why: The 2.0L can overfuel on cold starts, which floods the engine. Ford released a bulletin for this.
issues.next: Ask a shop to check for the cold-start bulletin and any engine computer update.

issues.t: Will not crank in Park but starts in Neutral
issues.sym: Nothing happens when you turn the key in Park, but the engine starts if you move the shifter to Neutral.
issues.why: The transmission range switch or its adjustment can stop telling the starter the car is in Park.
issues.next: Have the range switch adjusted or replaced. Until then, start in Neutral with your foot on the brake.

issues.t: Harsh shifts between gears
issues.sym: A hard bump on the 1-3 upshift or the 3-2 downshift.
issues.why: Ford issued bulletins for harsh shifts on the CD4E automatic, tied to internal servo parts and adaptive settings.
issues.next: Have the fluid checked and ask the shop about the bulletin repair before it gets worse.

issues.t: Manual transmission differential failure (V6)
issues.sym: Grinding or banging from the transmission, or the car will not move even though the engine runs and the clutch works.
issues.why: Ford found the differential gears in the V6 manual transmission could fail.
issues.next: Stop driving if it grinds or will not move. A tow and a transmission repair or replacement are usually needed.

issues.t: Shifter stuck in Park with the brake pressed
issues.sym: You press the brake but the shifter will not come out of Park, sometimes with a click.
issues.why: The brake-shift interlock or the brake light circuit can fail, so the car does not know the brake is pressed.
issues.next: Check whether your brake lights work. Have the interlock and brake light switch tested.

issues.t: Alternator failure and dead battery
issues.sym: The battery light comes on, lights dim, or the battery keeps going flat.
issues.why: The alternator wears out and stops charging. Owners also report replacing batteries before finding the real cause.
issues.next: Have the charging system tested before buying another battery.

issues.t: Anti-theft system prevents starting
issues.sym: The engine will not crank or starts and dies, and the theft light on the dash may flash.
issues.why: The passive anti-theft system (PATS) may not read the key. Magnets or other keys on the ring can interfere, and Ford has bulletins on no-start problems from this system.
issues.next: Try the engine with the key alone on the ring, then a spare key. If neither works, a shop or locksmith with Ford tools can diagnose and program keys.

issues.t: Heater core leak
issues.sym: A sweet smell inside, a greasy film on the windshield, damp carpet on the passenger side, or coolant loss.
issues.why: The heater core behind the dashboard can develop leaks. Ford issued a bulletin for heater core leaks.
issues.next: Have the cooling system pressure-tested. Fix it soon because low coolant can lead to overheating.

issues.t: Heat and A/C blow only from the defrost vents
issues.sym: Air comes out only at the windshield no matter which vent setting you choose.
issues.why: The vent doors are moved by vacuum. A cracked hose or a loose vacuum motor link sends air to the default defrost setting.
issues.next: Have the vacuum lines and vent door motors checked.

issues.t: Steering wheel shakes when braking
issues.sym: The steering wheel or brake pedal shudders when you slow down from speed.
issues.why: Uneven front rotor wear or thickness variation causes vibration. Ford issued a bulletin on diagnosing brake vibration.
issues.next: Have the front rotors measured; they may need machining or replacement with new pads.

issues.t: Front wheel bearing noise
issues.sym: A humming or growling noise that rises with speed and may change when you turn.
issues.why: The front wheel bearings wear out. Ford has a bulletin on noise that seems to come from them.
issues.next: Have the bearings checked for play. A badly worn bearing can overheat, so do not put it off.

issues.t: Clunk from the front stabilizer bar links
issues.sym: A clunk or knock from the front over bumps.
issues.why: The stabilizer bar links or bushings wear out. Ford has a bulletin on this front noise.
issues.next: Have the links checked. They are cheap and quick to replace.

issues.t: Power steering moan when turning
issues.sym: A groan or moan from the power steering, often when coming back from a right turn.
issues.why: Ford found power steering noise on these cars, including on the 2.5L V6.
issues.next: Check the power steering fluid level and look for leaks. Ask the shop about the bulletin repair.

issues.t: Rear disc parking brake sticks
issues.sym: The parking brake will not release fully, or a rear wheel feels hot or drags.
issues.why: On cars with rear disc brakes, the parking brake mechanism in the caliper can stick. Ford issued bulletins for this.
issues.next: Have the rear calipers and parking brake cables checked. A dragging brake wears pads quickly.

issues.t: Water leaking onto the front floor
issues.sym: Wet carpet on the front floor after rain or a car wash.
issues.why: Water can get past the plastic shield behind the door trim panel.
issues.next: Have the door water shield resealed. Dry the carpet to prevent mold.

issues.t: Temperature gauge reads high when the engine is not hot
issues.sym: The gauge sits higher than normal even though the engine is not overheating.
issues.why: Ford issued bulletins for gauges reading high in the normal range.
issues.next: Confirm the real engine temperature with a scan tool before assuming it is overheating.
